claims.name: Control master volume from a physical knob
claims.statement: A DJ can raise or lower the Mixxx master volume gain by turning a physical knob, without touching the software UI.

claims.name: See volume level on physical LEDs
claims.statement: A DJ can glance at three LEDs to gauge current master volume instead of watching a screen.

claims.name: Crossfade between two channels from a physical fader
claims.statement: A DJ can blend between two tracks using a physical crossfader rather than an on-screen control.

claims.name: Cue a channel privately in headphones
claims.statement: A DJ can preview either channel in their own headphones, without the audience hearing it, before mixing it into the main output.

claims.name: Not stated
claims.statement: Not stated in the available sources.

claims.name: Responsiveness of physical controls
claims.statement: Turning a knob or pressing a button should be reflected in Mixxx (and vice-versa for LEDs) without a noticeable lag, since this is used live while mixing.

attrs.scenario: DJ turns the gain knob during a live set

claims.name: Simplicity of setup for a hobbyist builder
claims.statement: The project is documented as a step-by-step wiring and install guide aimed at someone building it themselves, not a packaged commercial product.

attrs.scenario: A hobbyist follows the Readme to wire and flash their own unit

claims.name: DJ / builder
claims.statement: The person who both builds the hardware and uses it while mixing - in this project the same role, based on the Readme's first-person, self-build framing.

attrs.expectations: A working, low-latency physical control surface for Mixxx

claims.name: Must integrate with Mixxx's MIDI controller scripting API
claims.statement: Any control surface must speak MIDI and be expressed as a Mixxx controller mapping (JS + XML), since that is the only integration point Mixxx exposes.

attrs.rationale: Mixxx is third-party software; only its documented scripting API is available
attrs.impact: Forces every control's behaviour into a MIDI CC/Note vocabulary

claims.name: No app card or CMDB record exists
claims.statement: This system has no staged app card, manifest row, or any metadata beyond its own source and Readme, so nothing about it has been independently catalogued.

attrs.why_it_matters: Any programme-level tracking of this app depends entirely on this one analysis being current
attrs.mitigation: Stage a manifest-row.yaml or app card if this needs to be tracked alongside other apps

unknowns.looked_for: a measurable latency or performance target for control responsiveness
any stakeholder beyond the DJ/builder - e.g. other band/crew members, a venue, a hardware supplier
an app card or CMDB integrations list to cross-check against STR-003 (Mixxx)
unknowns.conclusion: no app card staged - see CTX-010
